function.arguments: {"finding": "The 'channel' column is not randomly assigned — the email campaign was deliberately targeted at existing high-value customers (loyal and returning), while paid_search targeted new customers. This creates a confounding: channel and customer_segment are systematically related. Comparing total revenue between channels without adjusting for customer_segment would attribute differences to the channel, when they may instead reflect the higher spending power of the targeted segments.", "implication": "A raw comparison of total revenue by channel is misleading. The higher revenue in email is likely due to targeting high-value customers, not the channel itself. A proper comparison must control for customer_segment, e.g., by stratifying or using a model. However, since the question asks only which channel produced the most revenue, and we have cleaned the data (removed refunds, parsed revenue correctly), we can report the raw totals — but with caution that the result is confounded."}
function.name: note_finding
